quotes.text: The only examples which have not been discussed in Sec. II B are those which occur when the elastic constant matrix has two or more irreducible representations of the same symmetry.

For example, the 2A1 representations in the hexagonal, or trigonal classes. In these cases, there is in general no acoustic wave whose velocity is zero when the elastic constant stability condition given in Table I is equal to zero.
In general, this is not the case and there is no requirement that an acoustic mode must have zero velocity when a stability condition is violated.

quote_normalization: Whitespace and line-wrap hyphens normalized; A1 subscript rendered inline.
conclusion: The listed repeated nontrivial representations have compatible zero-acoustic directions. Table I lists type 0; the examples quantify the acoustic eigenvalues and compatibility residuals. The crystal system 4/-4/4/m is tetragonal.
